dropped.reason: Unfixed CVE-2026-93753 (CVSS 8.7). Fix PR closed unmerged; no patched release exists. Migrate to @fastify/deepmerge.

rationale: Adopt @fastify/deepmerge as the primary implementation: it is the only candidate that combines OIDC trusted publishing, SLSA provenance, zero runtime dependencies, bundled types, active maintenance and immunity to CVE-2026-93753. deepmerge-ts is approved as the fallback for cyclic inputs or Map/Set merging, at the cost of a long-lived NPM_TOKEN in its release pipeline. deepmerge is dropped because the vulnerability has no upstream fix and is invisible to npm audit. ts-deepmerge, merge-deep, lodash.merge, @corex/deepmerge, deep-extend and the CVE-fork packages are rejected; defu, merge-anything and @75lb/deep-merge remain on hold and are not approved for this requirement.
decided_by: platform-security; revalidated by opencode-review (delegated by dbs-amoswong)
scope: Library selection and merge semantics. Application call-site migration and the deepmerge removal schedule are consumer obligations.
criteria: No unfixed high or critical advisories
Works from both CommonJS and ESM consumers

alternatives_considered.name: @fastify/deepmerge 3.2.4
alternatives_considered.reason: OIDC trusted publishing with SLSA provenance, zero dependencies, bundled types, active, fastest measured, and blocks all four CVE-2026-93753 variants.

alternatives_considered.name: deepmerge-ts 8.0.2
alternatives_considered.reason: Handles cycles and Map/Set, has strong inference and provenance, but publishes with a long-lived NPM_TOKEN rather than OIDC.

alternatives_considered.name: deepmerge 4.3.1
alternatives_considered.reason: Unfixed CVE-2026-93753, no release since 2023 and invisible to npm audit; migrate by 2026-12-31.

alternatives_considered.name: ts-deepmerge 8.0.0
alternatives_considered.reason: No CI or publish workflow and no provenance; fails the release-integrity constraint.

alternatives_considered.name: merge-deep 3.0.3
alternatives_considered.reason: No release since 2021, three dependencies expanding to 13 packages, no types and no provenance.

alternatives_considered.name: lodash.merge 4.6.2
alternatives_considered.reason: Frozen since 2019 and tied to lodash's advisory stream; no path to future fixes.

alternatives_considered.name: @corex/deepmerge 4.0.43
alternatives_considered.reason: No repository, no source review and no release since 2023.

alternatives_considered.name: deep-extend 0.6.0
alternatives_considered.reason: Unmaintained since 2018, no CI, no types and no provenance. The historical CVE-2018-3750 is fixed in 0.6.0, but the package is not maintained.

alternatives_considered.name: @stackline/deepmerge 1.1.0
alternatives_considered.reason: New single-maintainer fork with near-zero adoption and no independent review; its CVE fix is self-asserted.

alternatives_considered.name: defu 6.1.7
alternatives_considered.reason: Defaults semantics, not overwrite merge; no publish workflow and no provenance.

alternatives_considered.name: merge-anything 6.0.9
alternatives_considered.reason: ESM-only, one dependency, no declarations and no publish workflow.

alternatives_considered.name: @75lb/deep-merge 1.1.5
alternatives_considered.reason: Pulls lodash and typical, defeating the zero-dependency constraint; ESM-only and no types.

conditions: Use @fastify/deepmerge 3.2.4 as the default; pin it exactly and keep the lockfile.
Use deepmerge-ts 8.0.2 only when cyclic inputs or Map/Set merging are required; pin it exactly and record the NPM_TOKEN release gap.
Do not use deepmerge after 2026-12-31; migrate existing call sites to @fastify/deepmerge.
Keep the four-variant prototype regression in the test suite.
Configure array handling explicitly; @fastify/deepmerge concatenates arrays by default.
Use deepmerge-ts for cyclic input; @fastify/deepmerge does not detect cycles.
unknowns: The local benchmark measured the nested-config workload, not every application shape.
deepmerge-ts still authenticates with a long-lived NPM_TOKEN; provenance is present but the token remains a release risk.
@fastify/deepmerge is CommonJS-only and relies on ESM default-import interop.
The deepmerge migration call sites were not enumerated.
reversal_cost: Low: both approved packages use a small merge API, and the existing deepmerge wrapper is a thin layer.
review_triggers: A new advisory or bypass affects @fastify/deepmerge or deepmerge-ts.
Either package changes its release pipeline or loses provenance.
The deepmerge migration misses the 2026-12-31 deadline.
A cyclic-input requirement makes the fallback the primary.
A maintained zero-dependency alternative with better ESM support appears.
